nodes.name: RhPd-H solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The RhPd-H was synthesized through a one-pot solvothermal method by the simultaneous reduction of Rh(acac)3 and Pd(acac)2 in formaldehyde solution. Formaldehyde can be decomposed into hydrogen gas on metal catalysts (HCHO → H2 + CO), and then the in situ generated hydrogen molecules can be dissociated into H atoms on Pd surfaces.
nodes.source_text: The RhPd-H was synthesized through a one-pot solvothermal method by the simultaneous reduction of Rh(acac)3 and Pd(acac)2 in formaldehyde solution.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals dominant sheet-like morphology with roughly flat surface and some wrinkles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the RhPd-H was characterized by high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM, Figure 2a) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Figure S1). The products have dominant sheet-like morphology that presents a roughly flat surface, with some wrinkles.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms ultrathin character of RhPd-H nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ultrathin character was further confirmed by atomic force microscopy (AFM) images and corresponding height profiles (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows Rh and Pd are distributed uniformly through the sheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping show that the Rh and Pd are distributed uniformly through the sheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS peak at 4.46 eV confirms hydrogenation state of RhPd-H.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) was further performed to detect the hydrogenation state of the RhPd-H (Figures 2g and S3). The measured EELS peak was 4.46 eV, which matches well with results in reported metal-hydride systems.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows small shake up at 6 eV in valence spectra due to interaction between Rh/Pd 4d and H 1s states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The interaction between the Rh/Pd 4d and H 1s states results in a small shake up appeared at 6 eV in the valence spectra of the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurement (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution HAADF-STEM shows average lattice spacing of 0.230 nm, 3.6% larger than Rh6Pd4 alloy (0.222 nm), indicating H incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-resolution HAADF-STEM images indicate that the average lattice spacing of the RhPd-H is 0.230 nm (Figure 2h,i), which is about 3.6% larger than that expected for the normal Rh6Pd4 alloy nanostructures (0.222 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD peaks shift to lower angles indicating expanded crystal lattices due to interstitial H atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, the measured XRD peaks shifted to lower angles during the reaction, indicating the expanded crystal lattices (Figure 3h). This abnormal behavior also suggests that a substantial concentration of interstitial H atoms were confined in the products as they are formed.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the RhPd-H was characterized by high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM, Figure 2a) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Figure S1).
